newsitem.title: USA: Maine egg farm to pay $2 million fine.
newsitem.headline: Maine egg farm to pay $2 million fine.

text.p: A Maine egg farm accused of being an "agricultural sweatshop" will pay more than $2 million in fines to settle safety and wage violations, the Labour Department said Monday.

DeCoster Egg Farm, the nation's largest producer of brown eggs, was accused of forcing its employees, many of them Hispanic, to work in unsafe conditions and live in unsanitary onsite housing trailers.

"This settlement is a giant milestone for the workers at DeCoster Egg Farms. It says you should not have to risk serious injury or illness to earn a living to support your family," Labour Secretary Alexis Herman said in a statement.

Former Labour Secretary Robert Reich called DeCoster an "agricultural sweatshop" during a news conference last July where he showed videos of workers cleaning manure with their hands and raw sewage bubbling from bathtubs and sinks in the housing facilities.
Federal officials had originally sought $3.8 million in fines. The allegations prompted a consumer boycott, and at least two New England supermarket chains have stopped selling DeCoster's eggs.
Under the settlement, DeCoster also will pay $21,000 in back wages to 100 workers and will hire an independent monitor to make sure it complies with recordkeeping laws and improves workplace safety.

The privately owned farm has been repeatedly cited since the mid-1970s for safety, labour and environmental problems. The state of Iowa has also sued DeCoster for environmental violations at a pig farm the company owns in that state.

Reich's charges and the ensuing boycott prompted DeCoster to hire a team of Maine business officials to work on the farm's problems. But the officials soon resigned, saying owner Austin DeCoster was not willing to address their concerns.
